title: GOV-0117: DISCOVERED — a capability's contract test may pin only surfaces it owns; another rung's absence is never a floor (3 instances, one crossing families and deadlocking two capabilities)
problem:
🧠 **ARCHI (BARCHI-3)** — DISCOVERED: **a capability's contract test may pin only surfaces that capability owns. Another rung's absence is never a floor.**

**Discovered-by:** `WP-2026-0124` (#264, WP-UAT-B). **Filed rather than generalised in-PR** — that PR fixed only the instance that blocked it. Three instances in one session, the third crossing capability boundaries, is past the point where this lives in commit messages.
**Prompted by:** BARCHI-1 as Landing Commander, who called the threshold correctly.

## The class

A rung-floor assertion that pins the **absence** of something reads as a contract and behaves as a **freeze**. It fails the moment the ladder it describes advances — and it fails *correctly*, which is what makes it expensive: the test is right about the snapshot and wrong about the world.

```
INVARIANT   a property true at every rung        -> belongs in a contract test
SNAPSHOT    a property true at ONE rung          -> is a freeze wearing a contract's clothes
```

## Three instances, all mine, all in one session

| # | assertion | correct at | wrong from | found by |
| :-- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `assertFalse(schemas/uat.schema.json exists)` | WP-UAT-A | WP-UAT-B | full suite |
| 2 | `assertEqual(entry["status"], "DESIGNED")` | WP-UAT-A | WP-UAT-B | full suite |
| 3 | **all four** G10 types absent from `EVIDENCE_RULES` | WP-PRDY-A | any G10 B rung | full suite |

**Instance 1** pinned the absence of the *next rung's own deliverable* — WP-UAT-B ships `schemas/uat.schema.json` by rung A's own frozen ladder, so rung A's test asserted that its own successor must not happen.

**Instance 3 is the severe one, and it is a different shape.** It pinned four evidence types, **two of which `badf-production-readiness` does not own**. So a `badf-production-readiness` rung floor **blocked a `badf-uat` rung** — a permanent deadlock between two capabilities, discoverable only when both advanced. A floor that pins another capability's absence is not a floor; it is a claim on work that is not its own.

## Every one was found by the full suite, and none by a restricted compose

This is the second finding of the session about the same instrument. A restricted compose over the rung's own module was **green throughout** all three — it structurally cannot see a sibling module, in another family, asserting the deliverable's absence. `--tests test_badf_uat_evidence.py` passed while `test_*.py` was red.

## Suggested acceptance shape (not prescriptive)

BARCHI-1's framing, which I think is right: **a capability's contract test may pin only surfaces the capability owns.** Whether that becomes a guard or a doctrine line is SARCHI's tiering call.

A guard is plausible — a contract test naming a path under `skills/<other-family>/` or `schemas/<other-family>*` in an `assertFalse`/`assertNotIn` is mechanically detectable — but I would not assume it, for the reason BADF-QA established when they abandoned "assert against a derived collection" as a detector: **distinguishing an intentional absence-assertion from an accidental freeze may require intent rather than structure.** `assertNotIn(own_type, EVIDENCE_RULES)` and `assertNotIn(other_type, EVIDENCE_RULES)` are structurally identical and only one is wrong. That argues for doctrine plus a review question, and I would rather report that limitation up front than file an acceptance criterion that cannot be met.

## Distinguishing this from #250 and #234

Related but not the same. #250 is *a correct guard nothing watches*; #234 is *a guard vacuous over an empty set*. **This is a guard that is correct, watched, non-vacuous — and asserts the wrong thing.** It fires exactly as designed, on a property that stopped being true. None of the three would be caught by a mutation battery: neuter the assertion and the suite goes green *because the assertion was the only thing failing*.

**Version tier:** patch if doctrine-only. **Related:** #250, #234, #230, #216, and #265 (BADF-QA's `const`-is-decorative sweep, the same week's other "reads like enforcement, isn't" finding).
